messages:
Avery: Quick sync on where we draw the line between model manifests vs runtime for precision. Thinking: canonicalize allowed precisions and degradation budget in manifest so compile/runtime share one contract. Reactions?
Ravi: (+1) How do we still let customers tune per-tenant SLAs?
Avery: Manifests expose allowed_overrides and max_degradation. Runtime can accept overrides but must validate they are subsets of allowed_overrides and degradation <= max_degradation.
Maya: We need fields for operational decisioning too: latency_delta_estimate, cost_delta_estimate, quality_anchor_vector, and a validation_artifact_hash for CI.
Sam: For FP8 edge failures, propose an "early-fallback" trigger: monitor token-level degscore; if it exceeds threshold within first N tokens, switch to safer precision and optionally regenerate recent tokens.
Maya: Regeneration breaks streaming clients. Alternate: soft-correct—emit a corrective append or rerank, and expose a regenerate flag clients can opt into.
Ravi: Also: manifests must be versioned and signed for Dedicated/Private. Add migration playbook: pin by manifest_version during rollout, staged replacing with canary checks.
Avery: Minimal manifest sketch included in the RFC (in the thread): precision_candidates, degradation_budget, allowed_overrides, confidence_thresholds, fallback_policy_id, latency_delta_estimate, cost_delta_estimate, validation_artifact_hash.
Sam: Action items: Avery to draft RFC with schema + rollout plan; Ravi to write override-validation rules; Maya to define telemetry hooks for early-fallback degscore and smoke-check anchors; Sam to draft signing/versioning + migration checklist.
deploy-bot: Draft RFC created: /rfc/precision-manifest-boundary-v1 — reviewers: Avery, Ravi, Maya, Sam
